    """L1's want: [(category, [(name, title)])] in G-45 (d)'s order."""
    out = []
    for category in sorted(TABLE, key=str.casefold):
        items = [(stem, meta_name(stem)) for stem in TABLE[category]]
        items.sort(key=lambda item: (item[1].casefold(), item[0]))
        out.append((category, items))
    return out


def listed(client, project):
    """`list_graphics`' categories, or None and the error."""
    got = gp.attempt(client, "list_graphics", {"project": str(project)})
    if not got["ok"]:
        return None, got["error"]
    return reply(got).get("categories"), None


def outline(categories):
    return [(c.get("name"), [(g.get("name"), g.get("title")) for g in c.get("graphics") or []])
            for c in categories or []]


def clips_of(client, project):
    whole = reply(gp.attempt(client, "get_project", {"project": str(project)})).get("project") or {}
    clips = list(whole.get("clips") or [])
    return [c["graphic"]["name"] for c in clips if c.get("graphic")]


def modules_on_disk(project):
    folder = Path(project) / "graphics"
    return sorted(p.name for p in folder.glob("*.js")) if folder.is_dir() else []


def launch(app, look):
    HOME.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    log = WORK / f"framejob-{look}.log"
    if log.exists():
        log.unlink()
    launched = mcp.launch(str(app), arguments=["-RCDevAppearance", look],
                          env=bounded.child_env({"CFFIXED_USER_HOME": str(HOME)}),
                          log_path=str(log), timeout=CALL_BOUND)
    if launched.client is not None:
        print(f"  instance ({look}) PID {launched.child.pid} at {launched.socket_path}",
              flush=True)
    return launched, log


def fixture(client, name):
    package = WORK / f"{name}.framejob"
    shutil.rmtree(package, ignore_errors=True)
    made = gp.attempt(client, "new_project", {"path": str(package)})
    saved = gp.attempt(client, "save_project", {"project": str(package)})
    if not made["ok"] or not saved["ok"]:
        return None, f"new_project {made}; save_project {saved}"
    return package, None


def tool_rows(client, project):
    """L1, I1, L2, I2, I3, I4, I5 on `project`."""
    print("\n1 — list_graphics and insert_graphic", flush=True)
    want = template_categories()

    # L1
    categories, error = listed(client, project)
    graphics = [g for c in categories or [] for g in c.get("graphics") or []]
    sections = [(c.get("name"), g) for c in categories or [] for g in c.get("graphics") or []]
    well_formed = all(
        g.get("from") == "template" and g.get("ok") is True and g.get("category") == section
        and isinstance(g.get("description"), str) and g["description"].strip()
        for section, g in sections)
    check("L1 list_graphics with no project module: no This Project; Data & Time, Screencast, "
          "Social & YouTube, Titles & Text, each G-45 (c)'s templates by title then name; every "
          "graphic from template, ok, its section's category, titled by its meta.name, with a "
          "description",
          error is None and outline(categories) == want and len(graphics) == 23 and well_formed,
          f"error {error}; got {outline(categories)}; want {want}; well formed {well_formed}")

    # I1
    before = clips_of(client, project)
    got = gp.attempt(client, "insert_graphic",
                     {"project": str(project), "name": "lower-third", "from": "template"})
    after = clips_of(client, project)
    written = Path(project) / "graphics/lower-third.js"
    same = written.exists() and written.read_bytes() == (TEMPLATES / "lower-third.js").read_bytes()
    check("I1 insert_graphic {lower-third, template}: ok, name lower-third, graphics/lower-third.js "
          "byte-equal to the template, one clip more drawn by lower-third",
          got["ok"] and reply(got).get("ok") is True and reply(got).get("name") == "lower-third"
          and same and sorted(after) == sorted(before + ["lower-third"]),
          f"{got.get('error') or {k: reply(got).get(k) for k in ('ok', 'name')}}; bytes equal "
          f"{same}; clips {before} → {after}")

    # L2
    categories, error = listed(client, project)
    first = (categories or [{}])[0]
    ours = first.get("graphics") or []
    check("L2 list_graphics after: This Project first, holding exactly lower-third (\"Lower "
          "third\", from project, category Titles & Text); then L1's four",
          error is None and first.get("name") == "This Project"
          and [(g.get("name"), g.get("title"), g.get("from"), g.get("category"), g.get("ok"))
               for g in ours] == [("lower-third", "Lower third", "project", "Titles & Text", True)]
          and outline((categories or [])[1:]) == want,
          f"error {error}; got {outline(categories)}")

    # I2
    on_disk = modules_on_disk(project)
    before = clips_of(client, project)
    got = gp.attempt(client, "insert_graphic",
                     {"project": str(project), "name": "lower-third", "from": "project"})
    after = clips_of(client, project)
    check("I2 insert_graphic {lower-third, project}: ok, name lower-third, one clip more drawn by "
          "lower-third, graphics/*.js unchanged (no copy)",
          got["ok"] and reply(got).get("name") == "lower-third"
          and sorted(after) == sorted(before + ["lower-third"])
          and modules_on_disk(project) == on_disk == ["lower-third.js"],
          f"{got.get('error') or reply(got).get('name')}; clips {before} → {after}; graphics "
          f"{on_disk} → {modules_on_disk(project)}")

    # I3
    wrote = gp.attempt(client, "write_graphic",
                       {"project": str(project), "name": "broken", "source": BROKEN})
    before = clips_of(client, project)
    got = gp.attempt(client, "insert_graphic",
                     {"project": str(project), "name": "broken", "from": "project"})
    check("I3 a project module that does not compile is refused with \"graphics/broken.js does "
          "not compile: …\" and places nothing",
          wrote["ok"] and not got["ok"]
          and got["error"].startswith("graphics/broken.js does not compile: ")
          and clips_of(client, project) == before,
          f"write {wrote.get('error', 'ok')}; insert {got.get('error', 'NOT refused')!r}")

    # I4
    template = gp.attempt(client, "insert_graphic",
                          {"project": str(project), "name": "nope", "from": "template"})
    project_ = gp.attempt(client, "insert_graphic",
                          {"project": str(project), "name": "nope", "from": "project"})
    check("I4 an unknown name is refused naming it: from template listing lower-third among the "
          "templates, from project listing \"broken, lower-third\"",
          not template["ok"] and '"nope"' in template["error"]
          and "lower-third" in template["error"]
          and not project_["ok"] and '"nope"' in project_["error"]
          and project_["error"].endswith("broken, lower-third"),
          f"template {template.get('error', 'NOT refused')!r}; project "
          f"{project_.get('error', 'NOT refused')!r}")

    # I5
    bad = gp.attempt(client, "insert_graphic",
                     {"project": str(project), "name": "lower-third", "from": "file"})
    absent = gp.attempt(client, "insert_graphic", {"project": str(project), "name": "lower-third"})
    check("I5 from \"file\" is refused as \"from must be template or project (got \\\"file\\\")\"; "
          "no from is refused naming from",
          not bad["ok"] and bad["error"] == 'from must be template or project (got "file").'
          and not absent["ok"] and "from" in absent["error"],
          f"file {bad.get('error', 'NOT refused')!r}; none {absent.get('error', 'NOT refused')!r}")


def sheet_row(client, project, look):
    """U1 in `look`: the sheet up, captured, its dump read, cancelled."""
    before = clips_of(client, project)
    ran = gp.attempt(client, "perform_menu_item",
                     {"project": str(project), "path": ["Insert", "Graphic…"]})
    up = reply(ran).get("sheet") is not None
    picture = WORK / f"U1-{look}.png"
    shot = gp.attempt(client, "snapshot_ui",
                      {"project": str(project), "window": "sheet", "path": str(picture)})
    ids = []
    try:
        with open(reply(shot).get("layout_path") or "") as handle:
            ids = [v.get("id") for v in json.load(handle)["views"] if v.get("id")]
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
        pass
    missing = [i for i in IDENTIFIERS if i not in ids]
    cancelled = gp.attempt(client, "cancel_sheet", {"project": str(project)})
    down = (reply(cancelled).get("how") == "cancel_button"
            and "sheet" in reply(cancelled) and reply(cancelled)["sheet"] is None)
    png = picture.exists() and picture.stat().st_size > 0
    check(f"U1 ({look}) perform_menu_item Insert ▸ Graphic… puts the browser up; snapshot_ui "
          "writes its PNG and a layout dump holding the nine graphicbrowser identifiers; "
          "cancel_sheet presses Cancel and leaves no sheet; the clips are as before",
          ran["ok"] and up and shot["ok"] and png and not missing and down
          and clips_of(client, project) == before,
          f"performed {ran.get('error', 'ok')}, sheet {up}, snapshot {shot.get('error', 'ok')}, "
          f"png {png}, missing {missing}, problems {reply(shot).get('problems')}, cancel "
          f"{cancelled.get('error') or reply(cancelled).get('how')}")


def session(app, look, rows):
    """One instance in `look`: S0, the fixture, `rows(client, project)`, the
    close, then Z1 over its log. False when the instance, the home or the
    fixture failed."""
    launched, log = launch(app, look)
    made = False
    closed = None
    try:
        if launched.client is None:
            check(f"the {look} instance listens on its scratch socket", False,
                  f"no listening line for {launched.socket_path} in {log}")
            return False
        support = HOME / "Library/Application Support"
        check(f"S0 ({look}) the scratch home took: <home>/Library/Application Support is a "
              "directory", support.is_dir(), str(support))
        if not support.is_dir():
            return False
        project, why = fixture(launched.client, f"GB-{look}")
        made = project is not None
        check(f"the {look} fixture is made over MCP (new_project, save_project)", made, why or "")
        if made:
            try:
                rows(launched.client, project)
            except Exception as error:  # a row that could not run is a failure
                check("every row runs", False, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
            closed = gp.attempt(launched.client, "close_project",
                                {"project": str(project), "discard": True})
    finally:
        launched.stop()
        mcp.remove_scratch(launched.socket_path)
    lines = gp.complaints(log)
    check(f"Z1 ({look}) the project closes and grep \"Frame Job: \" over the log prints nothing",
          made and closed is not None and closed["ok"] and not lines,
          f"close {closed.get('error', 'ok') if closed else 'not reached'}; "
          + "; ".join(lines[:4]))
    return made


def mutate(sources, name):
    file, anchor, replacement, _ = APP_MUTANTS[name]
    text = (sources / file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    count = text.count(anchor)
    if count != 1:
        raise RuntimeError(f"anchor in {file}: expected once, found {count}")
    (sources / file).write_text(text.replace(anchor, replacement), encoding="utf-8")


def app_mutant(name):
    """Rule R: 0 the row FAILED in the copy, 1 it passed, 2 the control was
    not performed."""
    row = APP_MUTANTS[name][3]
    print(f"graphic browser — the {name} MUTANT ({row} must FAIL)", flush=True)
    made, reason = tree_copy.make_copy(str(WORK / "mutant"))
    if made is None:
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {reason}")
        return 2
    copy = Path(made)
    try:
        mutate(copy / "app/Sources", name)
    except (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {error}")
        return 2
    app, reason = tree_copy.build_app(copy, 1500)
    if app is None:
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {reason}")
        return 2
    session(proof_app.executable(app), "light", tool_rows)
    scored = {n.split()[0]: ok for n, ok in RESULTS}
    if row not in scored:
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {row} was not reached")
        return 2
    failed = [n.split()[0] for n, ok in RESULTS if not ok]
    caught = scored[row] is False
    print(f"{'MUTANT PASS' if caught else 'MUTANT FAILURE'}: {name} — {row} "
          f"{'FAILED' if caught else 'passed'} in the copy (failed: {', '.join(failed)})")
    return 0 if caught else 1


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--app", default=str(APP))
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", choices=sorted(APP_MUTANTS))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    app = Path(args.app)
    WORK.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    remove_leftovers()
    atexit.register(remove_leftovers)
    if args.mutant:
        return app_mutant(args.mutant)
    print("Spec §11 G-45 — the graphic browser: list_graphics, insert_graphic and the sheet",
          flush=True)
    if not app.exists():
        check("the app is built", False, str(app))
        print(f"\n0/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
        return 1

    def light(client, project):
        tool_rows(client, project)
        print("\n2 — the sheet over the dev tools", flush=True)
        sheet_row(client, project, "light")

    session(app, "light", light)
    session(app, "dark", lambda client, project: sheet_row(client, project, "dark"))
    good = sum(1 for _, ok in RESULTS if ok)
    print(f"\n{good}/{len(RESULTS)} checks passed")
    return 0 if RESULTS and good == len(RESULTS) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

`isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`, since this menu is `NSApp.windowsMenu` and
AppKit would otherwise list it a second time under its own title — Bring All
to Front), Help (Frame Job Help, Graphics Reference — road map 10's G5b: the
bundled `GraphicsAPI.md` opened in the person's own app, live while the
bundle holds it, with no document needed).
Road map 10's G5b adds **Insert**, right after Edit, holding **Graphic ▸**:
one item per bundled template (the twenty-three of `graphic/tests/graphics/`, copied
into the app's `GraphicTemplates/`, titled from the file stem —
`lower-third.js` is Lower Third — never by compiling it), a separator and
From File…; and File gains **Add Font to Graphics…** and **Add Image to
Graphics…** right after Consolidate Media…. None of the twenty-seven items takes a
key equivalent, for the caption items' reason; §11 G-16 has the rules.
Issue batch B84 (#103) adds, after a separator straight under Add Image to
Graphics… and before the separator above Export…, **Rename Graphic…**,
**Delete Graphic…** and **Restore Graphic Version…**, in that order and
with no key equivalents: each is one small sheet over the body its tool
runs (`rename_graphic`, `delete_graphic`, `restore_graphic`). Rename and
Delete are greyed in a project with no graphics, Restore when no version
of any graphic is kept, and Rename also while a nest is open; §11 G-30 has
the rules.
Grading GR4b puts **Adjustment Clip** first in Insert, above
Graphic ▸, with no key equivalent: one adjustment clip over the In/Out range,
else the selected clips' span, else the whole timeline, on the front track
when it takes the clip and is not a matte, else on a new front track named
"Adjustment"; one undo step, "Add Adjustment Clip", the new clip selected and
the inspector on Clip ▸ Color. It is greyed while a nest is open and when
there is nothing to cover (no range, no selection and an empty timeline);
§11 GR-6 has the rules.
----
its module's schema to animate, and none came with the op` for a value whose
module is missing or does not compile, while a `null` prop still removes. A
caller's own `schema` is refused by the argument gate as a stranger.

G5b gives the person the same doors (§9): File ▸ Add Font to Graphics… and
Add Image to Graphics… run the two imports' own body
(`GraphicStore.importFont` / `importAsset`), Help ▸ Graphics Reference opens
the file `graphic_reference` answers, and **Insert ▸ Graphic is
`write_graphic` of a template (or a chosen `.js`) then `add_graphic_clip`**
— one undo step, "Insert Graphic", placed by Add Text's rule (§11 G-16).

**Dev tools** (§11 V-1..V-3, road map 11). A tool compiled only under
`FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` — set for Debug and Release, never for Distribution, so
`make dist`'s binary holds none of their code (`dist_check.py`). A dev tool
is an ORDINARY tool: a handler and a catalog row from
`AgentServer+DevTools.swift`, spliced in before the file tools, covered by
the parity check and the argument gate like any other, and counted apart
from the ninety-eight product tools (`tools/proof/dev_tools.py`).
**`snapshot_ui {window?, view?, appearance?, path?, fill_preview?, layout?}`**
is the first. With no `window` it lists the visible windows (kind, class,
title, frame, content size, scale, occluded, key, main, the editor's project,
----
argument the table has never heard of, which is how a misspelt prose key is
caught rather than dropped in silence. App-state tools are skipped by the same rule
part 4 uses — the core's own op list, which has no row for a tool with no op
behind it. What no comparison of two lists can see is a
CALL. A call's KEYS are compared to the tool's published schema at the
dispatch — the argument gate, kpgalligan/framejob#21, for all ninety-eight
product tools — so a name no tool published is refused naming the tool and what it
takes, where it used to be dropped in silence; and that an argument the
catalog prints is one a hand-written handler really reads is put to the
running binary by `tools/proof/op_argument_proof.py`, one left-out argument
per op.

**GR-11 — Background render draws while Frame Job is left alone, and stops when you touch it**
- **Setup:** GR-9's, with Background render on at 5 s in Settings ▸ Playback, and Activity Monitor showing Frame Job's CPU and memory.
- **Do:** Open a COPY of `~/temp/testmotiongraphics/parive-promo.framejob`, park the playhead at 41.87 s, and leave Frame Job alone for 20 s. Press Shift once, wait 20 s, then play 10 s. Park at 41.87 s again, press ⌘H to hide Frame Job and wait 20 s with it hidden. Then show it, untick Background render and leave Frame Job alone for 20 s.
- **Expect:** CPU stays low for about 5 s after you stop, then rises, and falls at the Shift. Hidden, the CPU rises about 5 s after the ⌘H and stays up (a pass opts out of App Nap). Memory stays within a quarter of physical memory above the start. The play is visibly smoother than GR-9's first play. With the box unticked, the CPU stays low while Frame Job is idle.
- **Answer:** CPU low, then up, then down at the Shift, yes or no; smoother than GR-9's first play, yes or no; CPU up while hidden, yes or no; idle CPU low with the box off, yes or no; the memory figure before and at its highest.
- **Source:** #127 G6 phase 4 (spec §11 G-38); `tools/proof/background_render_proof.py` measures this by tool, not the keyboard path or the look.

**GR-12 — A dark gradient graphic shows no rings and no visible grain**
- **Setup:** a 1920×1080 project; your usual display brightness; View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full.
- **Do:** Insert ▸ Graphic ▸ From File… a module that fills the frame with a dark radial gradient, e.g. `raster_dither_proof.py`'s `band374` (`<radialGradient gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse" cx="960" cy="540" r="1100">`, `#2A4F3D` at the centre to `#0D1512` at the edge). Look at it in the preview, then save the frame (File ▸ Save Frame… as PNG) and open it in Preview at 100 %. Export it as `prores_422` and as `hevc_10bit`, and once as `h264`, and look at each in QuickTime Player at 100 %.
- **Expect:** in the preview, the saved PNG, the ProRes and the `hevc_10bit` file the gradient shades smoothly, with no rings or steps you can pick out, and no grain you can see at 100 % from your normal distance. The `h264` file may show its steps again: that is PR-13's recorded limit, not a defect.
- **Answer:** rings in the preview, yes or no; rings in the PNG, the ProRes, the `hevc_10bit`, the `h264`, each yes or no; visible grain anywhere, yes or no (and where).
- **Source:** #375 part 1 (spec §11 PR-13); `tools/proof/raster_dither_proof.py` measures the banding (B1–B4b) and the per-pixel noise each export keeps, not how it looks to a person on a display.

**GR-13 — The bundled templates look and move right**
- **Setup:** a 1920×1080 project with a video clip on it, a 1080×1920 project and a 1080×1080 project; View ▸ Safe Areas on; View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full.
- **Do:** In each project, insert each of the 23 templates (Insert ▸ Graphic ▸ …), over the clip in the 1080p project, then play each from its start to its end.
- **Expect:** smooth entrances and outros, readable text, and nothing drawn past the Safe guide's outer (90 %, title-safe) rectangle at any moment, in every project.
- **Answer:** for each template that fails, its name, the project (1080p, 1080×1920 or 1080×1080) and what is wrong: a jerky move, text you cannot read, or something past the outer rectangle.
- **Source:** owner 2026-10-29 (spec §11 G-44); `graphic/tests/templates.rs` measures that nothing outside title-safe moves at every fifth frame and that no frame warns, and that the last frame is bare, with defaults, every `enum` combination and every text property long, not how the motion looks.

## Mattes

**MAT-1 — A matte plays**
- **Do:** 1. Put a 1080p movie on a track and a large bold text clip on the track above it; give the text a motion preset or an action that moves it across the frame. 2. Track ▸ Matte ▸ Alpha with the text selected. 3. Play it at View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full, then at Quarter. 4. Switch the mode to Luma, then Inverted Alpha, and play again. 5. In a 3840×2160 project, put a full-frame shape filled with a slow black-to-white linear gradient (one edge to the other) over the movie, set its track to Matte ▸ Luma, and look at a still frame at Full; then set it to Matte ▸ Off and look at the gradient itself.
- **Expect:** only the movie shows, and only through the letters (outside them, the canvas background; with Inverted Alpha, the reverse); the window follows the text's movement frame for frame with no lag behind it; the letters' edges are clean at Full and at Quarter, with no fringe, flicker or banding; Luma shows the movie through the text's brightness; in step 5 the movie fades in smoothly across the frame, with no step or band you cannot also see in the gradient drawn on its own.

digit, and are at most 63 characters (`lower-third`, `title-2`).

Graphics draw only with the fonts bundled with Frame Job and the ones you add
to the project (see [Fonts and pictures](#fonts-and-pictures)), never with
the fonts installed on your Mac, so a project draws the same everywhere.

## Adding a graphic

**Insert ▸ Graphic** lists the bundled templates, then **From File…**:

| Item | What you get | Default length |
|---|---|---|
| Arrow Highlight | A rounded box drawn on around a spot, an arrow growing toward it from the side nearer the frame's centre, and a label at the arrow's tail | 90 frames |
| Bar Chart | A titled bar chart whose bars grow in turn, from comma-separated values and labels | 150 frames |
| Callout | A circle that draws itself on, with an arrow and a label, at a position on the frame | 90 frames |
| Chapter Card | A full-frame card: a large outlined chapter number, a kicker, an accent rule drawing across and the title rising into view | 120 frames |
| Countdown | A timer counting down (or up) one step a second inside a ring that empties or fills, pulsing on each tick and flashing at the end | 330 frames |
| Counter | A number counting from one value to another with thousands separators, a prefix and a label | 90 frames |
| Donut Chart | A titled donut whose slices sweep in turn from comma-separated values and labels, the first slice's share counting up in the centre, with a legend beside it (below it in portrait) | 150 frames |
| End Screen | A full-frame card with a title, two 16:9 placeholders for the videos you link, side by side, and a subscribe circle centred under them (a column in portrait) | 300 frames |
| Gauge | A dial with ticks whose accent arc and needle swing to a value, with the value counting up and its units and label | 120 frames |
| Handle Tag | An accent tile holding a generic glyph (play, camera, speech bubble, note or globe) and a pill with your @handle, at a corner | 120 frames |
| Keyboard Keys | A shortcut such as cmd+shift+4 as keycaps popping in, each pressed in turn, with ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ and the arrows drawn as symbols, and a label under them | 90 frames |
| Kinetic Type | A sentence shown word by word, each word springing in, with an accent colour | 150 frames |
| Line Chart | A titled line drawn on through comma-separated values, a dot popping at each point, an optional area fill and the last value called out | 150 frames |
| Logo Reveal | A full-frame card on which an accent bar sweeps across, revealing your logo image (or a text mark), then becomes a rule over a tagline | 120 frames |
| Lower Third | A name and subtitle that slide in and fade out, boxed or not, aligned left, centre or right | 150 frames |
| News Ticker | A band along the foot of the frame with a headline box and items, separated by "\|", crawling right to left | 300 frames |
| Progress Bar | A labelled bar on a plate whose fill grows to a percentage, the figure counting, with a shine across it, at the bottom, centre or top | 120 frames |
| Quote Card | A full-frame card with a large quote mark, the quote's lines fading up in turn, and the attribution sliding in | 150 frames |
| Social Popup | A notification card at a corner with a generic avatar and a handle (and, for a comment, its text), its heart, speech bubble or share arrow popping as the count ticks up by one | 120 frames |
| Step Badge | A numbered accent circle popping in at a corner, with a label panel wiping out from behind it | 90 frames |
| Subscribe Button | A subscribe button a cursor clicks: it turns to its done label with a check, and a bell pops in beside it and rings after a second click | 150 frames |
| Title Card | A title fitted to the frame and a kicker over a two-colour gradient, fading in and out | 120 frames |
| Window Frame | A browser or app window's frame — title bar, three dots, a title or an address field, an outline — to put over a screen recording on the track below; the window's inside stays clear | 150 frames |
| From File… | Asks for a `.js` module and copies it into the project | the module's own |

Each template's properties, as the Graphic sub-tab shows them:

| Template | Properties |
|---|---|
| Arrow Highlight | x and y (sliders from 0 to 1, the spot as a fraction of the frame), boxWidth and boxHeight (0.02–0.8 of the frame), shape (a pop-up: box+arrow, box, arrow), label, accent |
| Bar Chart | values and labels (comma-separated text), title, color |
| Callout | x and y (sliders from 0 to 1, a fraction of the frame's width and height), label, color |
| Chapter Card | number (0–99), kicker, title, background, accent |
| Countdown | from, to, format (a pop-up: seconds, m:ss, h:mm:ss), label, ring (a checkbox), accent |
| Counter | from, to, prefix, label, color |
| Donut Chart | values and labels (comma-separated text; a value below 0 counts as 0), title, accent |
| End Screen | title, videoA, videoB, subscribe (the three labels), background, accent |
| Gauge | value (held between min and max), min, max, label, units, accent |
| Handle Tag | handle, glyph (a pop-up: play, camera, bubble, note, globe), position (a pop-up of the four corners), accent |
| Keyboard Keys | keys (keys joined by "+": cmd, shift, opt or alt, ctrl, up, down, left, right, or any other key's name or character), label (empty hides it), theme (a pop-up: light, dark), position (a pop-up: bottom, center, top), accent |
| Kinetic Type | text, stagger (1–30), color, accent |
| Line Chart | values and labels (comma-separated text), title, area (a checkbox), accent |
| Logo Reveal | logo (an image from the project's graphic assets; none draws the mark), mark, tagline, background, accent |
| Lower Third | Title, subtitle, accent, size (12–200), boxed (a checkbox), align (a pop-up: left, center, right) |
| News Ticker | headline, items (separated by "\|"), speed (40–600, pixels a second at 1080p), background, accent |
| Progress Bar | value (0–100), label, showPercent (a checkbox), position (a pop-up: bottom, center, top), accent |
| Quote Card | quote (a text area), attribution, background, accent |
| Social Popup | kind (a pop-up: like, comment, share), handle, text (shown for a comment), count, position (a pop-up of the four corners), accent |
| Step Badge | number (0–99), label, position (a pop-up of the four corners), accent |

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V) does not carry graphic properties.

Copying and pasting a graphic clip (⌘C, ⌘V) pastes a clip that names its
module; the module's `.js` file, fonts and pictures are not copied. In a
project without that module, the pasted clip draws the red error card until
you add the module under the same name, for example with **Insert ▸ Graphic ▸
From File…** on a file of that name.

*Agents:* `paste_attributes` with `groups: ["graphic"]`.

## Fonts and pictures

Choosing one:

1. Copies the module into the project's `graphics/` folder under a free name
   (a second Lower Third becomes `lower-third-2`, and so on).
2. Places one graphic clip at the playhead, on the front track if it fits
   there, otherwise on a new track above everything. With a nest open, the
   clip goes on the nest's front track, or a new track inside the nest.
3. Selects the new clip so the inspector shows its Graphic sub-tab.

**From File…** names the module after the chosen file: the name is
lowercased, each run of characters other than a–z and 0–9 becomes one `-`,
dashes are trimmed from the ends, the result is cut to 60 characters, and an
empty result becomes `graphic` (so `My Title.js` becomes `my-title`). If that
name is taken, it gets `-2`, `-3` and so on.

On the timeline a graphic clip is labelled **Graphic**, with a `{}` glyph, and
has no filmstrip.

The clip's length and size come from the module's own `meta`
(`durationInFrames`, `width`, `height`) when it gives them; otherwise it is
5 seconds long and the canvas's size. A graphic is placed at Fit scale, like a
shape.

Placing the clip is one undo step, **Insert Graphic**. Copying the file into
the project is not undone. If the module doesn't compile, the file stays in
`graphics/`, no clip is placed, and an alert gives the first error and its
line. A file that isn't UTF-8 text is refused.

The menu items are greyed until the project's window is open.

content.content:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its menu title comes from its file name, never from running it (spec §11 G-16).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).

```json screen
{
  "title": "Insert Graphic",
  "project": "demo",
  "steps": [
    {"call": "perform_menu_item", "args": {"path": ["Insert", "Graphic…"]}}
  ],
  "captures": [{"name": "sheet", "window": "sheet"}],
  "after": [{"call": "cancel_sheet", "args": {}}],
  "expect": [{"capture": "sheet", "visible_text": "Insert Graphic"}]
}
```

The Graphic dialog (Insert ▸ Graphic…, spec §11 G-45) is where a person
picks a motion graphic to put on the timeline. The demo project holds one
graphic of its own, `lower-third`, so the dialog opens on This Project.

Under the title "Insert Graphic" are three panes side by side. On the left, a
bordered list of categories: "This Project" (selected, a grey row), then the
bundled templates' four, "Data & Time", "Screencast", "Social & YouTube" and
"Titles & Text". In the middle, a wider bordered list of the chosen
category's graphics by name — here the one, "Lower third", selected. On the
right, the preview: the chosen graphic playing over a grey checkerboard, at
the canvas's shape (16:9 for the demo), looping; under it the graphic's name
in bold and its one-line description in grey, cut short with "…" if it is
longer than the preview is wide. The capture catches whichever frame of the
loop was showing; early in Lower third's loop the bar may not have slid in
yet.

A line under the panes is empty until an Insert is refused; then it holds
the reason, word for word ("graphics/<name>.js does not compile: …"), and
the dialog stays open. That is not captured here.

Bottom left, "From File…", a square outlined button: it closes the dialog
and asks for a `.js` file instead. Bottom right, "Cancel" (Esc) and a blue
"Insert" (Return; a double-click on a graphic does the same). Insert is
greyed when no graphic is chosen.

In the light capture the sheet is white with black text, the lists white
with a thin grey border and the selected rows light grey. In the dark capture
the sheet is near-black with white text, the lists near-black with a thin
grey border and the selected rows dark grey; the checkerboard is the same
grey in both.

# tools/proof — driving a built Frame Job over MCP, and rendering its chrome offscreen

`CLAUDE.md`'s "Verifying a build" is the standard: the app is verified by
driving the built binary and comparing what it renders, not by reading
code. These are the scripts that do it — an MCP script per road-map-2 phase,
from phase 2 an offscreen-chrome script beside it, and for the fixes
`archive/remaining.md` records, `remaining_proof.py` over MCP and
`remaining_probe.py` offscreen — so a proof can be re-run after a later
change rather than believed on the strength of a paragraph.

`mcp.py` is a small MCP client (streamable HTTP over the app's Unix socket,
tools only, no dependencies) — `MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")` is enough to
`initialize`, list the tools and call one: `call(tool, **args)`, or
`call_with(tool, {…})` when an ARGUMENT is itself spelled `name`
(`add_track`, `set_track`, `add_marker`, `set_marker`, `nest`), since
`call`'s own first parameter is the tool's name; given a port number it
raises a `TypeError` naming MC4. `export(**args)` and `export_with({…})` are
`export` as the proofs knew it before spec §11 #326 made it answer an id at
once: a refusal raises, and the answer is the finished file's, followed
through `wait_export(export_id)` (it polls `export_status` every 0.2 s; a
`failed` or `cancelled` job raises `ToolError("export: <reason>")`, and past
its bound, by default the client's own `timeout` (600 s unless the
script set its own, the bound the blocking call had), it calls `cancel_export` and raises); an answer
with no `export_id`, an older build's blocking one, is returned as it is.
Every proof that expects the file on return goes through them. It is also
the launcher the proofs share
(road map 14's MC4): `scratch_socket()` makes a `0700` folder under `$TMPDIR`
and answers `<folder>/agent.sock` (refusing a path over 103 bytes),
`launch(binary, …)` starts an instance there in its own session with
`RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set, logging to `log_beside(socket)`, and waits for the
socket's line (`wait_listening`), `socket_pid` finds the pid listening at a
socket (`lsof -U`, read only), `target(argv)` is a proof's socket argument
(else `$RC_AGENT_SOCKET`), `remove_scratch` deletes a scratch folder under the
temp dir, and `LSREGISTER` is the one spelling of `lsregister`'s path. No proof
binds the person's own socket (spec §11 MC-6). It also guards the defaults
domain each instance shares with the owner (issue batch B83, #238): a script
whose session moved a key outside AppKit's `NS*`/`Apple*` families ends with
status 3 and `mcp: DEFAULTS MOVED …` last on stderr when no other Frame Job
shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does.
`harness/` is the offscreen renderer, described at the end.

**Ports in records.** Road map 14's MC4 deleted the app's TCP listener.
Before it every instance was reached on a TCP port, so the dated runs and
result tables below name ports (`phase9_proof.py 4853`, `--port 4941`,
`/tmp/reelcut-4823.log`): those are what ran then, and stay as written. Today
a proof against a running instance takes the instance's socket path, and one
that launches its own does so on a scratch socket.

through `wait_export(export_id)` (it polls `export_status` every 0.2 s; a
`failed` or `cancelled` job raises `ToolError("export: <reason>")`, and past
its bound, by default the client's own `timeout` (600 s unless the
script set its own, the bound the blocking call had), it calls `cancel_export` and raises); an answer
with no `export_id`, an older build's blocking one, is returned as it is.
Every proof that expects the file on return goes through them. It is also
the launcher the proofs share
(road map 14's MC4): `scratch_socket()` makes a `0700` folder under `$TMPDIR`
and answers `<folder>/agent.sock` (refusing a path over 103 bytes),
`launch(binary, …)` starts an instance there in its own session with
`RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set, logging to `log_beside(socket)`, and waits for the
socket's line (`wait_listening`), `socket_pid` finds the pid listening at a
socket (`lsof -U`, read only), `target(argv)` is a proof's socket argument
(else `$RC_AGENT_SOCKET`), `remove_scratch` deletes a scratch folder under the
temp dir, and `LSREGISTER` is the one spelling of `lsregister`'s path. No proof
binds the person's own socket (spec §11 MC-6). It also guards the defaults
domain each instance shares with the owner (issue batch B83, #238): a script
whose session moved a key outside AppKit's `NS*`/`Apple*` families ends with
status 3 and `mcp: DEFAULTS MOVED …` last on stderr when no other Frame Job
shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does.
`harness/` is the offscreen renderer, described at the end.

**Ports in records.** Road map 14's MC4 deleted the app's TCP listener.
Before it every instance was reached on a TCP port, so the dated runs and
result tables below name ports (`phase9_proof.py 4853`, `--port 4941`,
`/tmp/reelcut-4823.log`): those are what ran then, and stay as written. Today
a proof against a running instance takes the instance's socket path, and one
that launches its own does so on a scratch socket.

  holds exactly the 23 modules of `graphic/tests/graphics/`, byte-equal

  `harness/build.sh`'s swiftc line, with `app/Resources/Fonts`,
  `GraphicTemplates/` (from `graphic/tests/graphics/`) and `GraphicsAPI.md`
  (from `docs/graphics-api.md`) copied beside it — its `resourceURL`, where
  the app finds all three. It runs over two COPIES of GM and scores M1–M10:
  the probe builds (M1, a scored failure otherwise); the menu bar's Insert
  right after Edit and its Graphic submenu, each template's URL byte-equal
  to its source (M2); File's two items after Consolidate Media…, Help's

  target for the four editor selectors with no window, and Graphics

  (M4); the four validate false before `startGraphicStore()` and true after

  1 200 000 lasting 3 000 000, "Insert Graphic", level 0 after a run-loop

  (M7); `insertGraphic(from: "My Counter (v2).js", grouped: true)` →

content.content:
The last line is `<n>/<n> checks passed`, and the exit status is non-zero if
any failed. The log's `Frame Job agent socket listening at <dir>/agent.sock`
line says the instance is up (`not bound: <reason>` says why not), and the same
log is where the startup parity check would complain — `grep "Frame Job: "
<dir>/framejob.log` must print nothing before a proof run means anything.

**The EXACT tool count belongs to the newest phase's script**, because it is
what tells a stale binary on the port from the build under test: road map 7's
`op_argument_proof.py` asserts **97** since cut-by-transcript CT-4's
`get_transcript` (96 from CT-3's `transcribe_for_fillers`, 95 from CT-2's
`detect_fillers`, 94 from #326's `export_status` and `cancel_export`, 92 from
road map audio-sync AS-1's `sync_audio`, 91 from grading-3 T3-2's `set_media_color`, 90 from grading
GR4a's `add_adjustment_clip`, 89 from issue batch B84's three
graphics-file tools, 86 from B44's `close_project`, 85 from road map 10's
G4b, 82 from G4a, 79 from G3b, 77 from D3·5), and
every script before it keeps
a floor — phases 1 to 9's 63, 65, 68, 70, 71, 73, 73, 73 and 74, and road map
3's 75 — so a later phase's tools never fail an older proof.
That exact count is of PRODUCT tools: road map 11's dev tools are in a Release
catalog and not a Distribution one, so they are counted apart through
`dev_tools.py` (`op_argument_proof.py` section 1).
Road map 5's own proof landed AFTER D3 and asserts FLOORS for that reason:
`e1_proof.py` and `e2_proof.py` want `>= 77` and `>= 57` of this build, so a
later phase that adds a tool does not have to come back and edit them — and
`e1_proof.py`'s `== 75` / `== 55` for the REFERENCE build are exact, because
that tree is frozen at a commit.
**The sixth handover cost nothing**, which is the first time that has
happened to a handover that MOVED the number: road map 5's E1 had already
turned `recording_proof.py`'s 75 into a floor when it added two transition
tools, and road map 7's D3 adds no tool at all, so the 77 is the count the
catalog has carried since E1 and no older script had to be edited. Its PROSE
had drifted, though, and that is what D3·5 corrected:
`recording_proof.py`'s docstring, its section banner and one comment all
still called its 75 exact.
Road map 3's was the fifth handover and cost two rows in
one script, both in the same commit as the tool: `phase9_proof.py`'s `TOOLS`
became a `>=`, and its `APP_STATE_TOOLS` — asserted as an EXACT set, because
an op tool that lost its scope would leave the count right and the set
wrong — gained `record_screen`, the first scopeless tool to arrive after
that set was written. Before it, the handover had happened four times, each
time exactly as it was written down — phase 5 added
`normalize_clip`, took the exact count, and phase 4's `check` became a `>=`;
phase 6 added `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`, took the count
at 73, and phase 5's became a `>=` in the same commit; and phase 7 was the
first handover that cost NOTHING, because it added no tool at all — its
surface is new ARGUMENTS on two tools that already existed, so phase 6's own
`TOOLS = 73` stayed an exact assertion and needed no edit. Phase 8 was the
second such handover and cost nothing either, its three features having no
tool at all by design, so for two phases running THREE scripts asserted 73
exactly. **Phase 9 is what that cost.** `set_scope` is one new tool — view
state, not an op — so the count moved to 74 and all THREE of those exact
assertions had to become floors in one commit, where every earlier handover
touched one script. The sentence to take from it is not that three edits are
expensive but that an exact count left standing in an old script ACCUMULATES:
the next phase to add a tool pays for every script that took the number while
it was still current. It is not decoration:
the phase-4 count was checked against the two new tools taken out of the
catalog and the registry together, where it reads 68 — and it is not the
only check that notices. `check` never stops a run, so that build goes on to
fail every check that names either tool and then ABORTS at 4b's first
`export_captions`; the mutation paragraph below has the whole list.

budget and runs alone; R3 h264 books nothing;

for h264, nor for `av1` at a rate that cannot be stepped (no frame count). Q1 the live shared queue and ledger with physical = 4 × the sheet job's cost: a
headless Export… sheet writes W9 as `av1` Smaller while A (`av1`), B and C (`h264`) are
enqueued — A held with the exact sentence, B then C passing it and finishing before the

the sheet's finish is read at every queue and ledger notification, so a launch inside the
sheet's `end` reads after it); Q2 `export_status` for held A; Q3 at 1 TiB A runs beside a

# 04-impl-notes — graphic browser, phase 1 (lane-a, uncommitted)

## What was done
Done in the order the spec gives.
1. **Spec §11 G-45** was written first: it is in `designs/spec/11-decisions/graphics.md`. `11-decisions/README.md` gets the G-45 row, G-16's row now says "amended by G-45", and the graphics.md line count is updated.
2. **Templates:**
   - All 23 `graphic/tests/graphics/*.js` gained `category` and `description` in `meta`, after `name`. Nothing else in them changed. The descriptions are 42–64 characters, short enough to fit one line under the preview.
   - New `graphic/tests/template_meta.rs` holds the table and the one-line rule.
   - `docs/graphics-api.md` and `docs/graphics-api.d.ts` now document `category` and `description`.
3. **Shared insert bodies:**
   - New `ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift` has `writeGraphicModule(from:)` and `graphicClipMaker(named:)`, plus the shared sentence `noGraphicsFolderSentence`.
   - `EditorViewController.generatedClipOps(in:_:)` was extracted from `addGeneratedClip`. Its behaviour is unchanged, and `make typecheck` passed.
4. **Catalog and preview:**
   - New `GraphicCatalog.swift` holds `GraphicBrowserItem`, `GraphicBrowserCategory`, `GraphicCatalog` and `GraphicTemplateLibrary`. The library is NSLock-memoised; it compiles the templates once against the bundled fonts, through the now-internal `GraphicRegistry.compile`.
   - New `GraphicPreviewPlayer.swift`: one `Thread` with an 8 MiB stack and an `NSCondition`. Frame = ⌊elapsed×fps⌋ mod length, paced, skipping when slow. Rendering uses `AgentServer.graphicContext` (now internal) with props `{}` at `previewBudgetMs`. Frames go over the checker; the error card is used for a throw and for `.failed`. Delivery is a main hop, only for the newest generation. It exposes `thread` and `drawn` (frames, any drawn on main) for the probe.
5. **The sheet** is `GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift`:
   - 920 pt wide, panes 410 pt tall, two single-column view-based `NSTableView`s (180 and 240 pt), and a preview well at the canvas aspect ratio with a bold title and a one-line tail-truncated description under it.
   - The message label sits above the bottom bar.
   - The bottom bar holds From File… (`leading`), then Cancel (Esc) and Insert (Return).
   - It carries the nine `graphicbrowser.*` identifiers.
   - The preview column is a plain view with every edge pinned. A first version used an `NSStackView`, which `snapshot_ui` reported as ambiguous; this fixed it.
   - `viewDidDisappear` stops the player and runs a pending From File….
   - `showGraphicBrowser(_:)` presents the sheet with `presentAsSheet`. Its validator is `graphicStore != nil`, and the editor's generic attached-sheet guard covers V1.
6. **Wiring:**
   - The menu is "Graphic…" and `graphicMenu()` is removed.
   - `UIMenuTable` has `showGraphicBrowser: .sheet`.
   - `inventory.json`: the old selectors are gone and `showGraphicBrowser:` is added. There is a new presentAsSheet site at :34. The From File… panel site (:50) is now `reached_after` `showGraphicBrowser:` via the sheet's `viewDidDisappear`. `reportingGraphicFailure` (:162) is reached after `showGraphicBrowser:` via the panel's completion. Lines are re-keyed.
   - Agent side: new `AgentServer+GraphicBrowser.swift`; catalog rows after `restore_graphic`; two handler rows in the frozen `AgentServer.swift`; the `AssistantPrompt` graphics topic gains both tools; "ninety-eight" → "one hundred" in `AgentCatalog.swift` and `AgentServer+Gate.swift`. The `AgentCatalog.swift` list comment now says "the eleven of `AgentCatalog+Graphics.swift`", naming both new tools.
7. **Docs:**
   - Spec §9, §7.9c (G5b paragraph and both tools, and "one hundred" in its dev-tools sentence), §7.9a (count), and the spec README's line cells.
   - `designs/screens/15e-graphic-browser-sheet.md`.
   - In `docs/guide/`, `graphics.md` describes the dialog and This Project; its template table is now titled by `meta.name` with a Category column, and the From File… row became prose. `menus-and-shortcuts.md` and `mcp.md` (one hundred, two rows) are updated.
   - `docs/manual-checks.md` has the new GR-14, and CT-8, GR-4, GR-12 and GR-13 are re-pathed.
   - `CONTEXT.md` (Template; new **Category**) and `README.md` (Motion graphics highlight).
8. **Proofs:**
   - `graphics_menu_probe.swift`: M2–M5 and M6/M7 now go through the sheet. New rows M21–M32.
   - `graphics_menu_proof.py`: docstring, `PROBE_ROWS` M2–M32, and seven `browser-*` `PROBE_MUTANTS` under R1.
   - New `graphic_browser_proof.py`, with the `list-templates-only` APP_MUTANT.
   - `sheet_queue_probe.swift` V1 now lists the action as `showGraphicBrowser:`, and its `.py` docstring count went from twelve to eleven.
   - `op_argument_proof.py` `PRODUCT_TOOLS = 100`. `phase9_proof.py`, `recording_proof.py` and `recording_probe.py` have both tools in `APP_STATE_TOOLS`, with "thirty-eight" in their prose.
   - `tools/proof/README.md`: the count paragraph (100), sheet_queue V1 and the two re-pathed site rows, and a new section with the recorded run.

## Deviations from the spec
- **The does-not-compile sentence:** `graphicClipMaker` throws "graphics/<name>.js does not compile: …", as the Interfaces section says. The From File… path used to say "graphics/<name>.js was written but does not compile: …". G-45 (f) records the change, because a This Project graphic is never written. M9 still passes, since it only pins "does not compile".
- **No registry entry:** when `graphicClipMaker` finds no registry entry, it throws the store's `noModuleSentence` instead of "does not compile: no diagnostic".
- **Probe row numbering:** the spec named the rows by content. They are numbered M21–M32 in execution order, and the mutant rows follow from that: fallback M21, project-empty M22, project-last M23, insert-enabled M26, project-copies M30, skip-unique M7, player-kept M28. Each was confirmed as the first failure.
- **U1 is stricter:** it also requires `problems == []` in the layout dump. The spec asked only for the nine identifiers.
- **Tool description:** `list_graphics`/`insert_graphic` have no `scope` and are not in `offMainTools`. `insert_graphic` refuses a document with no editor or store using `ProjectDocument.noGraphicsFolderSentence`. That is the same text as the old body's sentence, now a constant.
- **AssistantPrompt topic wording:** the topic text was reworded ("graphics: write, rename, delete or restore a module; place and change a graphic clip; its reference, fonts and assets; insert a template"). F6 holds the search guide to 1500 characters, and the first wording came out at 1525. It is now at 1496.

## Files touched outside the Files list, and why
- `app/Sources/GraphicContactSheet.swift`: `paintChecker` changed from `private static` to `static`, a one-word change. The spec has the preview composite "over `render_graphic`'s checker", and this is the same kind of visibility change as the listed `compile` and `graphicContext` ones.
- `tools/proof/sheet_queue_probe.py`: its docstring said "twelve editor actions"; it now says eleven.

## Owed edits to CLAUDE.md files (not made here, as instructed; for the orchestrator)
- **Root `CLAUDE.md`:**
  - Rules, agent parity: "for all ninety-eight product tools" → "one hundred".
  - "Verifying a build": add `list_graphics` and `insert_graphic` to the app-state tool list, after `restore_graphic`.
  - The `roadmap`/ADR table needs nothing until the road map closes.
- **`graphic/CLAUDE.md`, the templates rule** (line ~128): "(Insert ▸ Graphic; …)" → "(Insert ▸ Graphic…; …)". Add that every template, the six fixtures included, declares `meta.category` (one of G-45 (c)'s four) and a one-line `meta.description` of at most 120 characters, held by `tests/template_meta.rs` (spec §11 G-45), and that a new template needs a row in its `TABLE`.
- **`app/CLAUDE.md`:**
  - **File map, new entries:**
    - `GraphicCatalog.swift`: G-45's list, one order for the sheet and `list_graphics`, plus `GraphicTemplateLibrary`, the templates compiled once per process, the first read on main, NSLock-memoised; the menu bar never reads it.
    - `GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift`: Insert ▸ Graphic…'s sheet. Insert calls the editor's bodies in-event (`applyEdit`), and a throw is shown word for word in `graphicbrowser.message`. `viewDidDisappear` stops the player and begins From File…'s panel (ReverseProgressSheetController's reason).
    - `GraphicPreviewPlayer.swift`: one 8 MiB `Thread` per player and an `NSCondition`; no AppKit or document off main; a main hop per frame for the newest subject only.
    - `ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift`: `writeGraphicModule`, `graphicClipMaker` and `noGraphicsFolderSentence`, shared by the sheet and `insert_graphic`.
    - `AgentServer+GraphicBrowser.swift`: `list_graphics` and `insert_graphic`.
  - **Changed roles:**
    - `+GraphicMenus` (line ~599): Insert ▸ Graphic… (`showGraphicBrowser`); `insertGraphicFromFile` is no longer an action and is called from the browser; `insertGraphic(from:grouped:)` and the new `insertProjectGraphic(named:grouped:)` delegate to the document bodies.
    - `+AddClips`: `static generatedClipOps(in:_:)`, the track choice alone, which `insert_graphic` uses.
    - `GraphicTemplates.swift` (line ~492): titles in the browser come from `meta.name`, and `title(for:)` is the fallback.
    - `GraphicRegistry.compile` is internal.
    - `AgentServer+GraphicRender.graphicContext` is internal.
    - `GraphicContactSheet.paintChecker` is internal.
    - The `graphics_menu_proof.py` mutant note (line ~2303): seven browser mutants now replace lines in `GraphicCatalog.swift`, `GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift`, `+GraphicMenus` and `ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift`.
  - **Rules, Hygiene:** the DispatchQueue/thread seam list needs "the graphic browser's preview player — one `Thread` per player (`GraphicPreviewPlayer.swift`) and its `DispatchQueue.main.async` frame hop". The best place is next to "the graphic prefetch's worker `Thread`s".
  - Line ~2653: "for all ninety-eight" → "one hundred".

## Notes and residue (nothing failing)
- **Frozen `AgentServer.swift`:** it went from 797 to 799 lines; only the two handler rows were added. Its `productHandlers` doc comment still says "thirty-six tools that are not ops … nine graphics tools", which is now 38 and eleven. That is prose in a frozen file and was not changed.
- **Stale "Insert ▸ Graphic" comments left in place:** `AgentServer+Graphics.swift`'s `add_graphic_clip` and `set_graphic` comments say "UI path: Insert ▸ Graphic" (lines 27 and 98), and `tools/proof/v2_menu_probe.swift`'s header says the templates give Insert ▸ Graphic its items. Neither file is in the Files list, so I left them.
- **`screens.py --only 15e-graphic-browser-sheet`** was run once against Debug. It captured light and dark with 0 new problems; the captures were looked at and are correct, and its run folder was removed. Its P2 row fails with "keys neither pinned nor in NOT_SHOWN ['RCCodecProbe', 'RCDevExportFault']". That failure is outside this change.
- **No Release-only failure found:** Release and Debug gave the same scores.
- **Leftovers:** the work folders were removed by each proof's exit. Nothing is committed.
